title: The Importance of Cells in Living Things

competencies.text: Describe how cells obtain nutrients and convert them into energy.

days.title: Cell Parts and Their Jobs
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will describe how cells obtain nutrients and convert them into energy.

🔬 Two Kinds of Cells

Prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have no nucleus; their DNA floats in the cytoplasm. Eukaryotic cells (plants, animals, fungi) have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

🧩 Organelles

OrganelleJobAnalogy
Cell membraneControls what enters and leavesSecurity gate
NucleusHolds DNA; directs cell activitiesPrincipal's office
CytoplasmFluid where many reactions occurWorkshop floor
MitochondriaRelease energy as ATPPower plant
RibosomesBuild proteinsAssembly line
Chloroplasts (plants)PhotosynthesisSolar panels
Cell wall (plants)Support and shapeBuilding frame
VacuoleStores water and materialsWater tank

🌿 Plant vs Animal Cells

Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Animal cells lack these, but both have a membrane, nucleus, mitochondria and ribosomes. Note: plants have mitochondria too — they need ATP like every cell.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
scenario.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make most of the cell's ATP.

scenario.text: Which structures are found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
scenario.explanation: Only plant cells have a rigid cell wall and chloroplasts for photosynthesis; both have the other parts.

scenario.text: Bacteria have no nucleus. Where is their DNA?
scenario.explanation: Prokaryotic cells have DNA in a region of the cytoplasm, not enclosed in a nucleus.

days.title: How Nutrients Enter Cells
days.content:
🚪 The Cell Membrane Is Selective

The membrane lets some substances pass and blocks others. Cells use several ways to move materials:

ProcessDirectionEnergy needed?Example
DiffusionHigh → low concentrationNoOxygen entering a cell
OsmosisWater moves to the side with more soluteNoRoots absorbing water
Facilitated diffusionHigh → low, through protein channelsNoGlucose entering red blood cells
Active transportLow → high concentrationYes (ATP)Root cells taking in minerals
EndocytosisMembrane wraps around large particlesYesWhite blood cell engulfing bacteria

🥒 Osmosis in Daily Life

Salting cucumbers for atchara pulls water out of their cells, making them limp. Putting wilted kangkong in plain water lets water move back in, making it crisp again. In both, water moves toward the side with more dissolved solute.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its meaning. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Particles spread from high to low concentration
match.why: It needs no energy from the cell.

match.right: Water moves across a membrane toward more solute
match.why: A special case of diffusion for water.

match.right: Moves substances from low to high using ATP
match.why: It works against the concentration gradient.
White blood cells use it to eat bacteria.

match.right: Selectively controls what enters and leaves

match.why: Water moves out toward the salty side.

days.title: Turning Nutrients into Energy
days.content:
🔋 From Food to ATP

Digestion breaks food into small molecules — mainly glucose. Blood delivers glucose and oxygen to every cell. Inside, cellular respiration releases the energy:

C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + ATP

🧭 Three Stages (simplified)

  1. Glycolysis (cytoplasm): glucose splits into two smaller molecules; a little ATP is made. No oxygen needed.
  2. Krebs cycle (mitochondria): these molecules are broken down further, releasing CO₂.
  3. Electron transport chain (mitochondria): uses oxygen to make most of the ATP; water forms.

⚡ Aerobic vs Anaerobic

AerobicAnaerobic
OxygenNeededNot needed
ATP per glucoseAbout 36–382
ProductsCO₂ and waterLactic acid (muscles) or alcohol + CO₂ (yeast)

Cells with high energy needs — muscle, heart and nerve cells — have many mitochondria.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Reason about cell transport and energy. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: During a marathon, a runner's muscle cells need much more energy. Which process speeds up MOST?

choices.label: Photosynthesis in the leg muscle tissue

scenario.explanation: To supply more ATP, muscle cells increase cellular respiration, which happens mostly in the mitochondria.

scenario.text: A raw potato slice is placed in very salty water for 30 minutes. It becomes soft and limp. Why?

choices.label: Water left the potato cells by osmosis
Salt entered and dissolved the cell walls
The potato absorbed water and burst open
Heat from the salt cooked the potato slice

scenario.explanation: The salty water had more solute, so water moved out of the potato cells, which lost firmness.

scenario.text: Root cells take in minerals even when the soil has fewer minerals than the roots do. Which process allows this?

choices.label: Osmosis of water toward the soil

scenario.explanation: Moving substances from low to high concentration requires energy — active transport.

scenario.text: Heart muscle cells have far more mitochondria than skin cells. What BEST explains this?

choices.label: The heart works nonstop and needs lots of ATP
Skin cells make their own sugar from sunlight
Mitochondria make the heart cells much heavier
Heart cells use mitochondria to store blood

scenario.explanation: Structure fits function: a constantly working organ needs many mitochondria to supply ATP.

scenario.text: A patient's cells cannot use oxygen properly. Which result is MOST likely?

choices.label: Much less ATP, so the patient tires quickly
More ATP, because glycolysis speeds up a lot
No change, because cells never need oxygen
More glucose is made by the mitochondria

scenario.explanation: Without oxygen, cells rely on anaerobic pathways that make only 2 ATP per glucose instead of about 36–38.

days.title: Why Cells Matter for Health
days.content:
🍚 Nutrition at the Cell Level

  • Carbohydrates (rice, kamote) → glucose, the main fuel for respiration.
  • Proteins (fish, monggo) → amino acids, used by ribosomes to build enzymes and tissues.
  • Fats → fatty acids, stored energy and part of cell membranes.
  • Iron → hemoglobin in red blood cells, which carry oxygen for respiration.

🩺 When Cell Processes Go Wrong

  • Anemia: too little hemoglobin → less oxygen reaches cells → less ATP → tiredness.
  • Dehydration: water lost by sweating or diarrhea upsets osmosis; cells cannot work well. ORS restores water and salts.
  • Cyanide poisoning: blocks the electron transport chain, so cells cannot make enough ATP.

🧠 The Big Picture

Every activity — thinking, moving, healing — depends on cells taking in nutrients through the membrane and turning them into ATP. Eating a balanced diet, drinking clean water and breathing clean air keep this cell machinery running.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: What is the energy currency of the cell?
escape.explanation: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) stores energy that cells spend for work.

escape.text: Which process moves molecules from LOW to HIGH concentration using energy?
escape.explanation: Only active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient, using ATP.

escape.text: Where in the cell does glycolysis take place?
escape.explanation: Glycolysis, the first stage of respiration, happens in the cytoplasm and needs no oxygen.

escape.text: Why does a person with iron-deficiency anemia feel tired?

choices.label: Less oxygen reaches cells, so less ATP is made
Their cells make too much ATP and overheat
Iron blocks glucose from entering all their cells

escape.explanation: Iron is needed for hemoglobin. Less hemoglobin means less oxygen delivered, reducing aerobic respiration.

escape.text: Which molecule do ribosomes use to build proteins?
escape.explanation: Proteins are chains of amino acids assembled by ribosomes.

escape.text: A child with diarrhea is given ORS. Which cell process does ORS mainly help restore?

choices.label: Water and salt balance for osmosis
DNA copying in the intestine cells
Protein building in the muscles only

escape.explanation: ORS replaces lost water and salts so cells can maintain proper osmotic balance and function.
